summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, and SVC syndrome was admitted with worsening symptoms of superior vena cava obstruction, including neck swelling, headache, blurry vision, and nausea. Imaging confirmed patent internal jugular veins, but a diagnostic SVC-IVC venogram revealed persistent SVC obstruction. An attempted stent placement was unsuccessful, and cardiothoracic surgery was consulted for future bypass planning. A blood culture showed coagulase-negative staph and Enterococcus faecium, but antibiotics were discontinued as the result was deemed a contaminant. Abdominal imaging indicated ileus related to a Crohn’s flare, managed conservatively. The patient improved symptomatically and was discharged home with a plan for outpatient surgical evaluation, medication adjustments, and follow-up.
